lessons.title: Responsible, fair and secure AI systems
lessons.summary: Assessing fairness readiness with sliced evaluation, monitoring for bias, and protecting data, models and inference traffic on Google Cloud.

sections.heading: What the exam guide asks
sections.body: Section 6.1 of the exam guide covers building secure AI systems (protecting against exploitation of data or models), aligning with Responsible AI practices (for example monitoring for bias), and assessing AI solution readiness (for example fairness and bias). Treat these as design-time and run-time checks, not one-off reviews.

sections.heading: Fairness readiness through sliced evaluation
sections.body: An aggregate metric can hide large gaps for subgroups. TFX **Evaluator** uses TensorFlow Model Analysis (TFMA) to compute **sliced metrics** (per region, device, age band and so on) and to gate a **candidate model against a baseline** before Pusher deploys it. The MLOps guide also calls for per-segment model validation before rollout. A model that improves overall but regresses on a protected slice should not be pushed automatically.

sections.heading: Bias monitoring in production
sections.body: Fairness can degrade after launch as the population shifts. Combine Model Monitoring drift and feature attribution signals with periodic sliced evaluation on fresh labelled data, and route regressions into the retraining pipeline.

sections.heading: Securing data and models
sections.body:
- **Sensitive data**: Sensitive Data Protection discovers and profiles data across BigQuery, Cloud SQL and Cloud Storage, inspects by infoType and de-identifies with masking, redaction, bucketing, date shifting or tokenisation. It can also analyse re-identification risk (k-anonymity) on BigQuery data.
- **Inference traffic**: a Private Service Connect dedicated private endpoint supports VPC Service Controls and is recommended for private production access. Dedicated public endpoints do not support VPC-SC, and VPC-peering private endpoints have no logging, streaming or encryption in transit.
- **Model supply chain**: Model Garden scans third-party models for malware, and organisation policies can restrict which models users can access.
- **Encryption and perimeters**: services such as RAG Engine and Workbench support CMEK and VPC-SC.

keyPoints: Fairness readiness = sliced evaluation plus gating, not only aggregate accuracy.
TFX Evaluator (TFMA) computes sliced metrics and compares candidate vs baseline.
De-identify PII before training with Sensitive Data Protection.
PSC dedicated private endpoints support VPC-SC; dedicated public endpoints do not.
Org policies can restrict Model Garden model access; third-party models are malware-scanned.

gotchas.trap: Approving a model because its overall AUC improved.
gotchas.correct: Check sliced metrics; an overall gain can hide a regression on a subgroup.

gotchas.trap: Putting a VPC-SC perimeter around a dedicated public endpoint.
gotchas.correct: Dedicated public endpoints do not support VPC-SC; use a PSC dedicated private endpoint.

gotchas.trap: Dropping the name column and calling the training data anonymised.
gotchas.correct: Use Sensitive Data Protection inspection and de-identification, and assess re-identification risk.

lessons.lab: Run a TFMA evaluation on a classifier sliced by a demographic-like column and compare metrics per slice. Then run a Sensitive Data Protection inspection job on a BigQuery table with synthetic PII and de-identify it with masking.

flashcards.front: Which BigQuery ML MODEL_TYPE builds a user-item recommender from interaction data?
flashcards.back: `MATRIX_FACTORIZATION` (collaborative filtering).

flashcards.front: Which BigQuery ML MODEL_TYPE forecasts a time series, and which variant adds external regressors?
flashcards.back: `ARIMA_PLUS`; `ARIMA_PLUS_XREG` adds external regressors. Plain `ARIMA` is being deprecated.

flashcards.front: What does the BigQuery ML TRANSFORM clause do at prediction time?
flashcards.back: It automatically reapplies the preprocessing defined at training, so callers pass raw columns. This prevents training-serving skew.

flashcards.front: Name two limits of the BigQuery ML TRANSFORM select list.
flashcards.back: No aggregations, UDFs or subqueries; and only TRANSFORM output columns are used for training.

flashcards.front: How do you make a BigQuery ML model available for online predictions on an endpoint?
flashcards.back: Set `MODEL_REGISTRY = 'VERTEX_AI'` in CREATE MODEL to register it in Model Registry, then deploy it to an endpoint.

flashcards.front: Which BigQuery ML model types handle dimensionality reduction?
flashcards.back: `PCA` and `AUTOENCODER` (an autoencoder can also flag anomalies by reconstruction error).

flashcards.front: What is a BigQuery ML remote model?
flashcards.back: A model created with a connection to an Agent Platform endpoint and queried from SQL; it has no fixed MODEL_TYPE and queries incur Agent Platform charges.

flashcards.front: Which model formats can BigQuery ML import?
flashcards.back: TensorFlow, TensorFlow Lite, ONNX and XGBoost.

flashcards.front: What does Model Garden offer?
flashcards.back: Discovery, testing, customisation and deployment of Google, partner and open models: foundation models, fine-tunable models, task-specific solutions and open-source models.

flashcards.front: How are Model Garden open models served?
flashcards.back: Deployed to an endpoint with serving containers such as vLLM, Hex-LLM, xDiT or Hugging Face, on GPUs or TPUs (Spot VMs or reservations are options).

flashcards.front: What are the stages of a RAG Engine pipeline?
flashcards.back: Ingest, transform/chunk, embed, index into a corpus, retrieve, and generate a grounded answer.

flashcards.front: What are the current names of Vertex AI Search and Vertex AI RAG Engine?
flashcards.back: Agent Search and RAG Engine, part of Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (the exam guide groups them under "Vertex AI Agent Builder").

flashcards.front: Which objectives does Agent Platform AutoML currently support?
flashcards.back: Tabular classification/regression and forecasting; image classification and object detection.

flashcards.front: What replaced AutoML Text and AutoML Video?
flashcards.back: Gemini prompting and tuning (AutoML Text shut down 2025-06-15; AutoML Video 2025-07-31).

flashcards.front: Which Google API extracts fields from invoices and forms without custom model training?
flashcards.back: Document AI, using pre-trained or customisable processors.

flashcards.front: What is the common signal of target leakage in an AutoML tabular model?
flashcards.back: Suspiciously high offline metrics driven by a feature that would not be known at prediction time.

flashcards.front: Where does Feature Store (V2) keep offline feature data?
flashcards.back: In BigQuery. BigQuery is the offline store, so no copy is needed. Feature Store adds a metadata layer, a feature registry and online serving.

flashcards.front: What backs online serving in Feature Store (V2)?
flashcards.back: Bigtable online serving. Optimized online serving is deprecated (2026-02-17); use Bigtable online serving or Vector Search for embeddings.

flashcards.front: What happened to Feature Store (Legacy)?
flashcards.back: Deprecated on 2026-02-17 and shut down on 2027-02-17. Migrate to Feature Store V2.

flashcards.front: Why put features in the Feature Store registry?
flashcards.back: So other teams can discover and reuse features instead of rebuilding them. Metadata is tracked in Knowledge Catalog (formerly Dataplex).

flashcards.front: Which TFX component stops training-serving skew in feature engineering?
flashcards.back: Transform (TensorFlow Transform). It produces one transformation graph used at both training and serving.

flashcards.front: What does the BigQuery ML TRANSFORM clause do at prediction time?
flashcards.back: It applies the preprocessing declared at CREATE MODEL automatically, so callers pass raw columns and skew is avoided.

flashcards.front: Four Sensitive Data Protection capabilities?
flashcards.back: Discovery and profiling (BigQuery, Cloud SQL, Cloud Storage), inspection by infoType, de-identification, and re-identification risk analysis such as k-anonymity.

flashcards.front: Name five de-identification techniques in Sensitive Data Protection.
flashcards.back: Masking, redaction, bucketing, date shifting and tokenisation.

flashcards.front: Which identity does a Workbench instance use to access data?
flashcards.back: The instance service account.

flashcards.front: Which identity does Colab Enterprise use by default?
flashcards.back: The user's own credentials.

flashcards.front: Is the Workbench executor supported with VPC Service Controls?
flashcards.back: No. The executor is not supported with VPC Service Controls.

flashcards.front: What happened to Workbench managed notebooks and user-managed notebooks?
flashcards.back: Both are retired. Managed notebook instances were deleted on 2026-03-30; user-managed notebooks became plain Compute Engine VMs on that date. Use Workbench instances.

flashcards.front: How do you run Spark from a Workbench instance?
flashcards.back: Through Managed Service for Apache Spark (formerly Dataproc).

flashcards.front: Two Model Garden governance controls?
flashcards.back: Third-party models are scanned for malware, and organisation policies can restrict which models users can access.

flashcards.front: What does an experiment in Experiments on Agent Platform group, and what does it log?
flashcards.back: Experiment runs and pipeline runs. It logs parameters, summary metrics and time-series metrics.

flashcards.front: Where are time-series metrics from Experiments stored?
flashcards.back: In managed (Vertex AI) TensorBoard.

flashcards.front: ROUGE vs adaptive rubrics in Gen AI evals?
flashcards.back: ROUGE is computation-based and needs reference answers. Adaptive rubrics are model-based (LLM judge), generate pass/fail tests per prompt, and need no references.

flashcards.front: Where can custom Python metrics run in Gen AI evals?
flashcards.back: Only in the SDK.

flashcards.front: Which workerPoolSpecs index holds the Reduction Server?
flashcards.back: Index 2, the slot otherwise used for parameter servers. Index 0 is the chief, 1 the workers, 3 the evaluators.

flashcards.front: What replicaCount must worker pool 0 have?
flashcards.back: Exactly 1. Pool 0 is the primary (chief) replica.

flashcards.front: Which environment variable is set on every replica of a custom training job?
flashcards.back: CLUSTER_SPEC. TF_CONFIG is set only for distributed jobs.

flashcards.front: What does Reduction Server do?
flashcards.back: It is an all-reduce algorithm that raises throughput and cuts latency when GPU workers exchange gradients across nodes.

flashcards.front: What do Reduction Server workers require?
flashcards.back: GPUs and NCCL-based data-parallel training in TensorFlow or PyTorch.

flashcards.front: What hardware do Reduction Server reducer nodes use?
flashcards.back: CPUs only, no GPUs. A machine such as n1-highcpu-16 is recommended. Reducer bandwidth should at least match worker bandwidth.

flashcards.front: Recommended Horovod setting with Reduction Server?
flashcards.back: Set HOROVOD_FUSION_THRESHOLD to at least 128 MB.

flashcards.front: Recommended PyTorch DDP setting with Reduction Server?
flashcards.back: Set bucket_cap_mb to 64.

flashcards.front: Which TPU generation does not support TensorFlow in custom training?
flashcards.back: TPU v6e (TensorFlow is not supported from v6e).

flashcards.front: What does JAX on TPU require in custom training?
flashcards.back: A custom container.

flashcards.front: Which environment variable does PyTorch/XLA need on TPUs?
flashcards.back: PJRT_DEVICE=TPU (enables the PJRT runtime; Google marks it as a v5e/v6e requirement).

flashcards.front: Default hyperparameter tuning algorithm?
flashcards.back: Bayesian optimisation (ALGORITHM_UNSPECIFIED), using Gaussian process bandits or linear combination search.

flashcards.front: When can you use GRID_SEARCH?
flashcards.back: Only when every parameter is INTEGER, CATEGORICAL or DISCRETE.

flashcards.front: How does a tuning trial report its metric?
flashcards.back: With the cloudml-hypertune package. Hyperparameter values arrive as command-line arguments.

flashcards.front: When do you choose UNIT_LOG_SCALE?
flashcards.back: When a range spans orders of magnitude, such as a learning rate. The range must be strictly positive.

flashcards.front: Explanation method for a tree ensemble?
flashcards.back: Sampled Shapley (works for non-differentiable models).

flashcards.front: Explanation method for a neural network or low-contrast images such as X-rays?
flashcards.back: Integrated gradients.

flashcards.front: What is XRAI best for?
flashcards.back: Region-based explanations of natural images. It builds on integrated gradients.

flashcards.front: Which models support example-based explanations?
flashcards.back: TensorFlow models only; not tree models, PyTorch or XGBoost.

flashcards.front: When does Vertex Explainable AI shut down, and what replaces it?
flashcards.back: Deprecated 2026-03-16, shuts down 2027-03-16. Google suggests open-source SHAP or LIME.

flashcards.front: SFT vs preference tuning vs RLFT: what data does each use?
flashcards.back: SFT: labelled prompt/response pairs. Preference: chosen and rejected responses. RLFT: dozens to a few hundred prompts plus up to 16 weighted reward functions.

flashcards.front: Which tuning method suits verifiable tasks such as SQL generation?
flashcards.back: Reinforcement learning fine-tuning (RLFT) with reward functions that check correctness.

flashcards.front: LoRA vs full fine-tuning?
flashcards.back: LoRA (PEFT) is cheaper and needs less data. Full fine-tuning can give higher quality but costs more to train and serve.

flashcards.front: What is Vertex AI Training called now?
flashcards.back: Agent Platform Managed Training (Vertex AI became Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform on 2026-04-22).

flashcards.front: How are Model Garden open models tuned and billed?
flashcards.back: With notebooks or pipelines, billed at custom training rates.

flashcards.front: Managed pipelines without running Kubeflow on GKE?
flashcards.back: Agent Platform Pipelines: serverless, runs Kubeflow Pipelines SDK or TFX pipelines compiled to YAML.

flashcards.front: Which serving pattern fits nightly scoring of a full table where no user waits for the result?
flashcards.back: Batch inference (an Agent Platform batch job, or ML.PREDICT for BigQuery ML models). It needs no deployed endpoint, so nothing sits idle.

flashcards.front: Do Agent Platform batch inference jobs autoscale?
flashcards.back: No. max_replica_count is ignored, so size the job with the starting replica count.

flashcards.front: What input sources does Agent Platform batch inference accept?
flashcards.back: JSONL, CSV and TFRecord files (optionally gzip), a Cloud Storage file list, or a BigQuery table.

flashcards.front: Where can batch inference write results?
flashcards.back: Cloud Storage or BigQuery, in the same region as the model.

flashcards.front: Which BigQuery ML function runs batch inference inside BigQuery?
flashcards.back: ML.PREDICT. It works for built-in models and for imported ONNX, TensorFlow, TensorFlow Lite and XGBoost models.

flashcards.front: How do you get low-latency online predictions from a BigQuery ML model?
flashcards.back: Register it in Model Registry (MODEL_REGISTRY = 'VERTEX_AI') and deploy it to an endpoint. No export is needed.

flashcards.front: What Apache Beam transform does Dataflow ML use for inference?
flashcards.back: RunInference. It works in batch and streaming pipelines, and it can swap in updated models (through side inputs) without stopping the pipeline.

flashcards.front: What does the default alias mean in Model Registry?
flashcards.back: It marks the version that is used when no version is specified, usually the production version.

flashcards.front: Prebuilt XGBoost container: required artifact file name?
flashcards.back: model.bst or model.joblib, exactly.

flashcards.front: Prebuilt scikit-learn container: required artifact file name?
flashcards.back: model.joblib

flashcards.front: Prebuilt PyTorch container: required artifact?
flashcards.back: A model archive named model.mar.

flashcards.front: Custom serving container: which address and port must the server listen on?
flashcards.back: 0.0.0.0, on the port in AIP_HTTP_PORT (default 8080).

flashcards.front: Custom container: request and response shape on the predict route?
flashcards.back: A POST with {"instances": [...], "parameters": {...}}; return {"predictions": [...]}.

flashcards.front: How do you A/B test or canary a new model version without changing client URLs?
flashcards.back: Deploy it to the same endpoint and use traffic split, raising its share gradually.

flashcards.front: What is a rolling deployment?
flashcards.back: Replacing a deployed model with a new version of the same model, reusing the existing compute.

flashcards.front: Can you change a deployed model's machine type in place?
flashcards.back: No. Most deployment settings, including machine type, cannot be changed after deployment, so you redeploy (for example, a new deployed model plus a traffic shift). Only some resources can be updated in place.

flashcards.front: Which endpoint type is the only option for tuned Gemini models?
flashcards.back: The shared public endpoint.

flashcards.front: Which endpoint type is recommended for private production access, including from on-premises and inside VPC-SC?
flashcards.back: A Private Service Connect (PSC) dedicated private endpoint.

flashcards.front: What do VPC peering private endpoints lack?
flashcards.back: Traffic split, request logging, streaming and encryption in transit.

flashcards.front: Dedicated public endpoint vs shared public: payload and timeout limits?
flashcards.back: Dedicated: up to 10 MB and a 1 h timeout. Shared: 1.5 MB and 60 s. Limits change, so check the docs.

flashcards.front: Default autoscaling targets on Agent Platform endpoints?
flashcards.back: CPU utilisation 60% and GPU duty cycle 60%. The platform scales on whichever is higher. Request count per replica is off by default.

flashcards.front: Why can a high maxReplicaCount cause quota errors?
flashcards.back: Quota is reserved for maxReplicaCount, not for the replicas that are running.

flashcards.front: What happens to requests while a scale-to-zero (Preview) deployment is scaled down?
flashcards.back: They get HTTP 429 and are dropped while a scale-up starts.

flashcards.front: What is a deployment resource pool?
flashcards.back: Model co-hosting: several deployments share VMs. It needs the same prebuilt TF or PyTorch container image and does not support AutoML models or custom containers.

flashcards.front: What does the optimized TensorFlow runtime offer?
flashcards.back: Faster, lower-cost TF inference. It is backward compatible with the prebuilt TF Serving containers, so you switch the container image without changing model code. Gains vary by model.

flashcards.front: Which online serving option should new Feature Store designs use?
flashcards.back: Feature Store V2 (BigQuery offline store) with Bigtable online serving, and Vector Search for embeddings. Legacy and Optimized online serving are deprecated.

flashcards.front: MLOps level 0
flashcards.back: Manual, notebook-driven training and hand-off deployment; infrequent releases, no CI/CD, high risk of training-serving skew.

flashcards.front: MLOps level 1
flashcards.back: Continuous training: the whole pipeline is deployed and retrains automatically, with data validation, model validation and metadata.

flashcards.front: MLOps level 2
flashcards.back: CI/CD of the pipeline itself: pipeline CI, pipeline CD, automated triggering, model CD and monitoring.

flashcards.front: Schema skew in a CT pipeline: what happens?
flashcards.back: Stop the pipeline so the team can investigate (for example missing features or wrong types).

flashcards.front: Value skew in a CT pipeline: what happens?
flashcards.back: Significant shifts in feature distributions are a signal to retrain the model.

flashcards.front: Five retraining triggers in the MLOps guide
flashcards.back: On demand, on a schedule, when new data is available, when performance degrades, when data distributions shift.

flashcards.front: Offline model validation checks
flashcards.back: Compare the candidate with the current production model, including per-segment performance, before any online test.

flashcards.front: Online model validation
flashcards.back: Canary or A/B test of the new model on a share of live traffic before full rollout.

flashcards.front: Pipeline CI tests
flashcards.back: Unit tests of feature engineering logic, checks that training converges, checks for NaN values.

flashcards.front: Model CD checks
flashcards.back: Target infrastructure compatibility, load and latency tests, quality thresholds versus the current model.

flashcards.front: Agent Platform Pipelines in one line
flashcards.back: Serverless service that runs KFP or TFX pipelines compiled to YAML, recording parameters and artifacts in ML Metadata (formerly Vertex AI Pipelines).

flashcards.front: Which SDKs author Agent Platform pipelines?
flashcards.back: Kubeflow Pipelines (KFP) SDK or TFX SDK.

flashcards.front: Google Cloud Pipeline Components
flashcards.back: Prebuilt pipeline components for Google Cloud services, such as AutoML training, so you do not write custom code.

flashcards.front: How do you run a pipeline on a recurring basis?
flashcards.back: Use the Agent Platform Pipelines scheduler API (create, pause, resume, delete schedules).

flashcards.front: TFX ExampleValidator
flashcards.back: Detects anomalies in data using the outputs of StatisticsGen and SchemaGen.

flashcards.front: TFX Transform
flashcards.back: Feature engineering with TensorFlow Transform; the same transform graph is used at training and serving, preventing skew.

flashcards.front: TFX Evaluator
flashcards.back: Computes TFMA sliced metrics and blesses a candidate only if it meets the configured thresholds, including comparison with a baseline model.

flashcards.front: TFX InfraValidator
flashcards.back: Loads the model in a sandboxed serving environment to confirm it can serve before pushing.

flashcards.front: What runs TFX data processing at scale on Google Cloud?
flashcards.back: Apache Beam on Dataflow (Beam can also run on Flink or Spark).

flashcards.front: BigQuery ML TRANSFORM clause
flashcards.back: Preprocessing defined at training is applied automatically at prediction and evaluation, so callers pass raw columns.

flashcards.front: Cloud Composer
flashcards.back: Managed Apache Airflow; fits when ML steps sit inside wider Airflow-orchestrated data workflows.

flashcards.front: Hybrid or multicloud pipelines
flashcards.back: Kubeflow Pipelines on your own Kubernetes runs KFP definitions outside Google Cloud; Agent Platform Pipelines is the managed option on Google Cloud.

flashcards.front: What does ML Metadata record for pipeline runs?
flashcards.back: Parameters and artifacts of each step, producing lineage graphs (can sync to Knowledge Catalog).

flashcards.front: Experiments on Agent Platform
flashcards.back: Groups experiment and pipeline runs; logs params, summary metrics and time-series metrics (stored in managed TensorBoard).

flashcards.front: Model Registry default alias
flashcards.back: Marks the version treated as production; deploy by alias instead of hard-coded version IDs.

flashcards.front: Register a BigQuery ML model without export
flashcards.back: Set MODEL_REGISTRY = 'VERTEX_AI' (plus VERTEX_AI_MODEL_ID) in CREATE MODEL.

flashcards.front: Status of legacy AI Platform Pipelines
flashcards.back: Shut down on 2025-01-31; use Agent Platform Pipelines.

flashcards.front: Training-serving skew vs prediction drift: what is the baseline for each?
flashcards.back: Skew: the training dataset. Drift: earlier production data. Drift detection works without training data.

flashcards.front: Model Monitoring v1: what is it scoped to?
flashcards.back: An Agent Platform endpoint. Its settings are shared by all models deployed on that endpoint. v1 is GA.

flashcards.front: Model Monitoring v2: what is it scoped to, and what does it add?
flashcards.back: A model version. It supports batch and online inference and models served outside Agent Platform; its objectives are input feature drift, output inference drift and feature attribution. It is in Preview.

flashcards.front: Default Model Monitoring v1 alert threshold?
flashcards.back: 0.3 per feature, with email alerts.

flashcards.front: How do you reduce Model Monitoring cost on a high-traffic endpoint?
flashcards.back: Lower the sampling rate (and choose a sensible monitoring frequency, which also sets the analysis window).

flashcards.front: Distance metrics used by Model Monitoring?
flashcards.back: Categorical: L-infinity (v1, v2) or Jensen-Shannon divergence (v2). Numerical: Jensen-Shannon divergence.

flashcards.front: What does feature attribution drift detect?
flashcards.back: A change in which features drive predictions (SHAP-based attributions), even when input distributions look similar. A Model Monitoring v2 objective.

flashcards.front: Explainable AI method for tree ensembles?
flashcards.back: Sampled Shapley (non-differentiable models; any custom model and AutoML tabular).

flashcards.front: Explainable AI method for neural networks or low-contrast images like X-rays?
flashcards.back: Integrated gradients.

flashcards.front: Explainable AI method for region-level saliency in natural images?
flashcards.back: XRAI, which builds on integrated gradients.

flashcards.front: Feature attributions are relative to what?
flashcards.back: A baseline you choose. A bad baseline gives misleading attributions.

flashcards.front: Example-based explanations: how do they work and what do they support?
flashcards.back: Nearest-neighbour search on embeddings; TensorFlow models only. Used for debugging, outlier detection and active learning.

flashcards.front: Status of Vertex Explainable AI?
flashcards.back: Deprecated 2026-03-16, shutting down 2027-03-16. Suggested replacements: open-source SHAP or LIME. Still on the exam guide.

flashcards.front: How do you assess fairness readiness before deployment in TFX?
flashcards.back: Evaluator (TFMA) computes sliced metrics per subgroup and gates the candidate model against the baseline before Pusher.

flashcards.front: Which tool de-identifies PII in BigQuery training data?
flashcards.back: Sensitive Data Protection: inspection by infoType, then masking, redaction, bucketing, date shifting or tokenisation; plus k-anonymity risk analysis.

flashcards.front: Which endpoint type supports VPC Service Controls for private production inference?
flashcards.back: A Private Service Connect (PSC) dedicated private endpoint. Dedicated public endpoints do not support VPC-SC.

questions.scenario: A retail analytics team stores two years of order history in BigQuery. Analysts know SQL but have no ML engineering experience. They need a churn classifier within a week and want to avoid moving data.
questions.stem: What should they do?
options: Train a BigQuery ML model with MODEL_TYPE = 'KMEANS' and label each cluster as churn or not churn.
Export the table to Cloud Storage as CSV and write a custom TensorFlow training job.
Train a BigQuery ML model with MODEL_TYPE = 'LOGISTIC_REG' (or a boosted tree classifier) directly on the BigQuery table.
Deploy an open model from Model Garden and prompt it with each customer row.
questions.explanation: BigQuery ML trains classification models in place with SQL, which matches a SQL-skilled team, a short timeline and the no-data-movement requirement. LOGISTIC_REG and BOOSTED_TREE_CLASSIFIER are supervised classifiers listed among CREATE MODEL types.
rationales: KMEANS is unsupervised clustering; it does not learn the churn label.
Custom training adds data movement and engineering effort the team does not have.
Correct: a supervised BigQuery ML classifier trained where the data lives fits the skills and timeline.
Prompting an LLM row by row is costly, slow and not a calibrated tabular classifier.

questions.scenario: A team trains a BigQuery ML model that bucketizes age and normalizes income in a SQL view before training. In production, a microservice calls the model with raw values and accuracy drops sharply.
questions.stem: What is the most maintainable fix?
options: Duplicate the bucketizing and normalization logic in the microservice before each call.
Switch to AUTOML_CLASSIFIER, which ignores preprocessing differences.
Retrain more often so the model adapts to raw values.
Move the preprocessing into the CREATE MODEL TRANSFORM clause and retrain so prediction calls can pass raw columns.
questions.explanation: Preprocessing defined in the TRANSFORM clause is stored with the model and applied automatically during evaluation and prediction, which removes training-serving skew. Duplicating logic in clients is a classic skew source.
rationales: Duplicated logic drifts over time and is exactly how skew starts.
AutoML does not reconcile inputs transformed differently at training and serving.
Retraining does not fix the mismatch between transformed training inputs and raw serving inputs.
Correct: TRANSFORM keeps one definition of preprocessing for training and serving.

questions.scenario: A bank built a BOOSTED_TREE_CLASSIFIER in BigQuery ML for fraud scoring. The card authorization system now needs predictions in milliseconds per transaction.
questions.stem: What should the ML engineer do?
options: Run ML.PREDICT queries from the authorization system for each transaction.
Rebuild the model as a remote model pointing at itself.
Export predictions nightly to Cloud Storage and look them up at authorization time.
Recreate the model with MODEL_REGISTRY = 'VERTEX_AI' so it registers in Model Registry, then deploy it to an Agent Platform endpoint.
questions.explanation: Setting MODEL_REGISTRY = 'VERTEX_AI' registers a BigQuery ML model in Model Registry without manual export, and from there it can be deployed to an endpoint for online inference. Query-per-transaction and nightly batches do not meet per-transaction online latency needs.
rationales: Per-transaction SQL queries are not designed for millisecond online serving.
Remote models call an existing endpoint; they do not create online serving for a BigQuery ML model.
Nightly precomputation cannot score new transactions as they happen.
Correct: register the model and serve it from an online endpoint.

A linear regression on date ignores seasonality and autocorrelation that time-series models handle.

AUTOENCODER

questions.scenario: An HR team wants a chatbot that answers employee questions from policy documents in Cloud Storage and Google Drive. The policies change monthly, and answers must reflect the latest version.
questions.stem: What is the most appropriate design?
options: Supervised fine-tuning of a Gemini model on the policy documents every month.
Create a RAG Engine corpus from the Cloud Storage and Drive sources and generate answers grounded on retrieved chunks.
Train an AutoML text classifier that maps questions to policy sections.
Prompt a Gemini model with no context and instruct it to say "check the handbook" when unsure.
questions.explanation: RAG Engine ingests from Cloud Storage and Google Drive, chunks, embeds and indexes content into a corpus, then retrieves relevant chunks to ground generation, so refreshing the corpus keeps answers current. Tuning adapts behaviour and is a poor way to inject frequently changing facts.
rationales: Monthly retuning is costly and still does not ground answers in the current text.
Correct: RAG keeps answers grounded in the latest documents.
AutoML Text is shut down, and classification would not produce answers.
Ungrounded prompting cannot answer from private policies.

questions.scenario: An AutoML tabular model predicting loan default shows near-perfect validation AUC, but performs poorly in production. Feature importance is dominated by a column named collections_agency_assigned.
questions.stem: What is the most likely cause and fix?
options: Underfitting; increase the training budget.
Target leakage; remove the column because it is only populated after a default occurs, then retrain.
Class imbalance; duplicate the minority class rows.
Serving latency; deploy to more replicas.
questions.explanation: A feature known only after the outcome inflates offline metrics and is unavailable or meaningless at prediction time; Google calls this data (target) leakage, which produces excellent evaluation metrics but poor real-world performance. Removing it and retraining gives an honest model.
rationales: Near-perfect validation metrics indicate the opposite of underfitting.
Correct: classic leakage pattern, fixed by dropping the post-outcome feature.
Imbalance would not produce near-perfect validation AUC driven by one post-outcome column.
Latency does not affect prediction quality.

questions.scenario: A retail company has three ML teams. Each team computes its own version of "customer 90-day spend" from the same BigQuery tables, and the numbers disagree. Leadership wants one governed definition that every team can find and reuse, without building another copy of the data.
questions.stem: What should the ML engineer recommend?
options: Register the feature in Agent Platform Feature Store (V2), which uses the existing BigQuery data as the offline store and exposes it through the feature registry
Export the feature to CSV files in Cloud Storage and share the bucket with all three teams
Create Feature Store (Legacy) entity types and run a nightly import job from BigQuery
Ask each team to document its SQL in a shared wiki page and agree on one version

rationales: Correct. V2 uses BigQuery as the offline store and adds a registry for reuse.

questions.scenario: Two models, a classifier and a regressor, are deployed on the same Agent Platform endpoint with Model Monitoring v1. The team wants hourly monitoring for the classifier and daily for the regressor, with different feature thresholds.
questions.stem: What is the issue and the best fix?
options: v1 monitoring settings apply to all models on an endpoint; use Model Monitoring v2 per model version (or separate endpoints)
v1 does not support classifiers; switch the classifier to AutoML
Thresholds can only be set to the default 0.3; contact support
Monitoring frequency must match the traffic split percentage
questions.explanation: In v1, monitoring configuration is shared by all models on an endpoint, so two different schedules are not possible on one endpoint. v2 is configured per model version, which allows separate settings.
rationales: Correct: v1 settings are endpoint-wide; v2 attaches to a model version.
v1 does not exclude classifiers.
0.3 is the default, not a fixed value.
There is no rule tying monitoring frequency to traffic split.

questions.scenario: A credit team uses a gradient-boosted tree model on Agent Platform and must give per-feature reasons for each decision.
questions.stem: Which Explainable AI attribution method should they choose?
options: Integrated gradients
XRAI
Sampled Shapley
Example-based explanations
questions.explanation: Sampled Shapley suits non-differentiable models such as tree ensembles. Integrated gradients and XRAI need differentiable models, and example-based explanations do not support tree models.
rationales: Integrated gradients requires a differentiable model such as a neural network.
XRAI is for image regions and builds on integrated gradients.
Correct: Sampled Shapley handles non-differentiable models like boosted trees.
Example-based explanations return similar examples, support TensorFlow only and not tree models.

questions.scenario: A hospital trains a TensorFlow CNN on low-contrast chest X-rays and wants pixel-level attributions to show radiologists which areas influenced a prediction.
questions.stem: Which method is the best fit?
options: Sampled Shapley
Jensen-Shannon divergence
Example-based explanations
Integrated gradients
questions.explanation: Integrated gradients is recommended for differentiable models and specifically for low-contrast images such as X-rays. XRAI targets natural images, and Sampled Shapley is aimed at non-differentiable models.
rationales: Sampled Shapley targets non-differentiable models and is costly for large pixel feature spaces.
Jensen-Shannon divergence is a drift metric, not an explanation method.
Example-based explanations show similar training images, not pixel attributions.
Correct: integrated gradients suits neural networks and low-contrast images.

questions.scenario: An image classifier explanation returns attributions concentrated on dark background pixels. The data scientist used an all-black image as the baseline, and many training images have dark backgrounds.
questions.stem: What should be checked first?
options: Whether Model Monitoring drift thresholds are too low
Whether the endpoint has enough replicas
Whether the baseline is appropriate, because attributions are relative to the chosen baseline
Whether the model should be retrained on grayscale images
questions.explanation: Feature attributions are computed relative to a baseline. A baseline that resembles real input regions can distort attributions, so validating or changing the baseline is the first step.
rationales: Drift thresholds are unrelated to per-request attributions.
Replica count affects throughput, not attribution values.
Correct: attributions depend on the baseline; an unsuitable one gives misleading results.
Retraining is premature before checking the explanation configuration.

questions.scenario: A churn model's input feature distributions are stable on Model Monitoring dashboards, yet accuracy has dropped. Analysts suspect the model now leans heavily on a different feature than at launch.
questions.stem: Which monitoring objective best surfaces this?
options: Input feature drift with a lower threshold
Feature attribution monitoring in Model Monitoring v2
Endpoint latency alerts
Skew detection on a single numerical feature
questions.explanation: Feature attribution monitoring tracks changes in SHAP-based attributions, revealing shifts in which features drive predictions. Input drift may stay quiet when marginal distributions look similar.
rationales: Lowering thresholds on stable inputs mainly adds noise and does not track importance.
Correct: v2 feature attribution monitoring detects shifts in feature importance.
Latency is an operational metric, not model behaviour.
Skew on one feature compares it with training data and does not capture importance shifts.

questions.scenario: A loan-approval model shows higher overall AUC than the current production model. Compliance requires that no applicant subgroup gets worse before rollout. The team uses TFX on Agent Platform Pipelines.
questions.stem: Which steps best meet this requirement? (Select two.)
options: Configure Evaluator (TFMA) with slices for the relevant subgroups
Remove subgroup columns from evaluation data so the model cannot be unfair
Rely on overall AUC because it already includes every subgroup
Have Evaluator gate the candidate against the baseline model so Pusher only deploys when slice thresholds pass
questions.explanation: TFMA sliced metrics reveal subgroup gaps that aggregate metrics hide, and Evaluator can block Pusher unless the candidate meets thresholds against the baseline. Dropping subgroup columns removes the ability to measure fairness.
rationales: Correct: sliced evaluation surfaces per-subgroup performance.
Without subgroup columns you cannot measure fairness; proxies can still encode bias.
An aggregate gain can hide a regression on a subgroup.
Correct: candidate-vs-baseline gating stops a model that regresses on a slice from being pushed.

questions.scenario: In late 2026 a team is starting a multi-year project that needs feature attributions for a scikit-learn model. An architect proposes building on Vertex Explainable AI.

Plan for open-source SHAP or LIME, because Vertex Explainable AI is deprecated with a 2027 shutdown
Use example-based explanations, which are the replacement for feature attributions
Avoid explanations entirely, since Agent Platform no longer supports them

questions.scenario: A bank serves a model to internal applications, including some on-premises. Security requires that inference traffic stay private and inside a VPC Service Controls perimeter, with request logging enabled.
questions.stem: Which endpoint type should they use?
options: Dedicated public endpoint
Shared public endpoint
Private Service Connect dedicated private endpoint
Private endpoint using VPC Network Peering
questions.explanation: A PSC dedicated private endpoint is recommended for private production access including on-premises, supports VPC-SC and supports logging. Dedicated public endpoints do not support VPC-SC, and peered private endpoints lack logging.
rationales: Dedicated public endpoints do not support VPC Service Controls.
Shared public endpoints are public and not suited to this requirement.
Correct: private access, VPC-SC and logging are all supported.
VPC-peered private endpoints do not support logging, streaming or encryption in transit.

questions.scenario: A healthcare team wants to train a model on BigQuery tables that contain names, phone numbers and dates of birth. Policy says identifiers must be removed or transformed before training, and they must quantify re-identification risk.
questions.stem: Which service should they use?
options: Sensitive Data Protection for inspection, de-identification and k-anonymity risk analysis
Model Monitoring skew detection
Explainable AI Sampled Shapley
Cloud Storage object versioning
questions.explanation: Sensitive Data Protection inspects data by infoType, de-identifies it with techniques such as masking, bucketing, date shifting and tokenisation, and analyses re-identification risk on BigQuery data.
rationales: Correct: it covers discovery, de-identification and re-identification risk.
Model Monitoring watches production inputs; it does not protect training data.
Attribution methods explain predictions; they do not de-identify data.
Versioning keeps object history and does not remove identifiers.

questions.scenario: A team at MLOps level 1 has an automated training pipeline in Agent Platform Pipelines. They want production monitoring to drive continuous evaluation and retraining.
questions.stem: Which signals are appropriate automated triggers for the training pipeline? (Select two.)
options: A developer edits a notebook cell
Model Monitoring detects a significant distribution shift
Model performance on fresh labelled data drops below a threshold
The endpoint URL changes
questions.explanation: The MLOps guide lists performance degradation and significant distribution shifts among triggers for continuous training, alongside on-demand, scheduled and new-data triggers. Notebook edits and endpoint URL changes are not model-quality signals.
rationales: Notebook edits belong to experimentation, not production retraining triggers.
Correct: distribution shift is a documented retraining trigger.
Correct: performance degradation is a documented retraining trigger.
Traffic split and rolling deployments keep the endpoint URL stable; it is not a quality signal.

questions.scenario: A BigQuery ML model applies scaling and bucketing in SQL during training. The application team reimplements the same logic in Java for online requests, and Model Monitoring now reports skew on those features.
questions.stem: What change best removes the root cause?
options: Retrain the model more often
Raise the skew thresholds for the affected features
Switch to drift detection so the alerts stop
Define preprocessing in the CREATE MODEL TRANSFORM clause so it is applied automatically at prediction time
questions.explanation: With a TRANSFORM clause, preprocessing defined at training is applied automatically during prediction and evaluation, so callers pass raw columns and skew from duplicated logic disappears. The other options hide the alert rather than fix the cause.
rationales: Retraining does not fix inconsistent serving logic.
Raising thresholds masks real skew.
Switching to drift hides a genuine training-serving mismatch.
Correct: TRANSFORM keeps training and serving preprocessing identical.

questions.scenario: A platform team wants to stop data scientists from deploying arbitrary third-party models from Model Garden into production projects.
questions.stem: Which control best addresses this?
options: Use organisation policies to restrict which Model Garden models users can access
Rely only on Model Garden malware scanning
Enable Model Monitoring drift detection on every endpoint
Disable endpoint request logging
questions.explanation: Organisation policies can restrict which models users can access in Model Garden. Malware scanning is useful but does not enforce which models are allowed.
rationales: Correct: org policies restrict model access centrally.
Scanning checks for malware but does not limit which models can be used.
Monitoring detects data changes after deployment, not unapproved models.
Disabling logging reduces visibility and does not prevent deployment.
